mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds after the recent dip, weekday foot traffic will follow with a lag and lift RETAIL_REC over the next month. The mechanism is direct commuter spillover into nearby shops and eateries.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -0.1 at t-1w to -9.9 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC stayed near -9
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A short-term rise in GROCERY_PHARM relative to RETAIL_REC indicates household errand substitution toward essential trips, which suppresses discretionary retail visits over the next 1-2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains at least 35 points above baseline while RETAIL_REC stays below -5
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is consistently above 40 across all four weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week average during weeks when GROCERY_PHARM stays above 35 and RETAIL_REC remains below -5.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls while WORKPLACES also weaken, the combined signal implies fewer trips into activity centers, so retail mobility declines over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest when both series move down together.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops below -7 and WORKPLACES drops below -5 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved to -7.4 at t-0w and WORKPLACES to -9.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean within four weeks after a week when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are below the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A regime of reduced transit access or mobility restrictions would transmit quickly into lower retail visits because shopping trips depend on public-transport connectivity. The mechanism activates only when TRANSIT declines sharply from one week to the next.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 2 points week-on-week from an already negative level
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -5.4 at t-1w to -7.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks after a qualifying TRANSIT drop, or if retail rises despite repeated transit contractions.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility means people are spending more time near home, which crowds out discretionary retail outings and keeps RETAIL_REC subdued over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive at 6.1 to 7.7 while RETAIL_REC stayed near -9
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above 6 for most weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility stabilizes or rises after a prior dip, it signals improved outdoor activity and generally better discretionary movement conditions, which should spill into higher retail visitation within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 3 points from a recent trough
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -21.9 at t-2w to -17.6 at t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks after PARKS rises by at least 3 points from its recent low.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increases contact intensity near business districts, and retail follow-through should appear after a one-week lag. The effect requires both commuting proxies to move up together.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week after at least one negative week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both weakened at t-0w after earlier improvement
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not move above its prior week after a week in which both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increase.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, simultaneous weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES should produce an outsized retail decline because access and commute-based demand both contract at once. The signal is conditional on both series staying depressed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT is below -5 and WORKPLACES is below -5 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES were negative at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days after two consecutive weeks with both proxies below -5.
